2607.25630.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Corpus for LLM-Based Simplification of Scientific Summaries
2607.25630.paper_summary: Interdisciplinary research is accelerating, yet scientific papers remain difficult to understand outside their home fields. We study large language model (LLM)-based simplification of scientific texts and present a human-in-the-loop workflow that transforms expert summaries into more accessible versions for non-specialists. Using SciSummNet as the source corpus, we first generate baseline simplifications with GPT-4o-mini. In Phase 1, readers from STEM fields outside computer science identify difficult sentences and phrases and compare the original and GPT-simplified summaries in terms of comprehensibility, naturalness, and simplicity. In Phase 2, computer science experts use this feedback to create expert-edited reference simplifications. We release the resulting corpus together with human judgments and automatic evaluation results. The Phase 1 judgments show a clear preference for the GPT-generated summaries in terms of comprehensibility and simplicity, while qualitative analysis of the Phase 2 edits highlights the importance of preserving domain-specific terminology and the strength of scientific claims. The resulting resource supports the training and benchmarking of simplification systems for cross-disciplinary scientific communication.
2607.25630.paper_summary_zh: 跨學科研究正在加速進行，但科學論文在其本領域之外仍然難以理解。我們研究基於大型語言模型（LLM）的科學文本簡化，並提出一種人機協作的工作流程，將專家摘要轉換為對非專家更易於理解的版本。以SciSummNet作為源語料庫，我們首先使用GPT-4o-mini生成基準簡化版本。在第一階段，來自計算機科學以外的STEM領域的讀者識別困難的句子和短語，並在可理解性、自然性和簡單性方面比較原始摘要和GPT簡化的摘要。在第二階段，計算機科學專家利用這些反饋創建專家編輯的參考簡化版本。我們釋放了最終的語料庫，並附上了人類評價和自動評估結果。第一階段的評價顯示，在可理解性和簡單性方面，對GPT生成的摘要有明顯的偏好，而第二階段編輯的質性分析強調了保持領域特定術語和科學主張強度的重要性。最終資源支持了跨學科科學交流的簡化系統的訓練和基準測試。
